builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Agent-Native by Design: A Programming Language for Agentic Applications
summary: Jac replaces hand-written glue code over SDKs/agent frameworks by embedding typed LLM calls, tool use, workflow state, and model-guided routing into a Python-superset language with shared execution semantics. The cost is adopting a new language/runtime and its ecosystem constraints, with compiler-visible control flow offered as the main mechanism for optimization claims. It can fail if the promised analyses, speculative execution, or service partitioning do not preserve behavior under real workloads, or if the smaller ecosystem and tooling maturity increase delivery risk.
rationale: The claimed benefit is reduced integration code and development effort rather than direct runtime efficiency on a single 24GB GPU, so production adoption should wait for independent validation and ecosystem maturity.
technique: Agent-native programming language (Jac) with typed LLM operations

claims.statement: Jac replaces hand-written glue code over SDKs/agent frameworks by embedding typed LLM calls, tool use, workflow state, and model-guided routing into a Python-superset language with shared execution semantics. The cost is adopting a new language/runtime and its ecosystem constraints, with compiler-visible control flow offered as the main mechanism for optimization claims. It can fail if the promised analyses, speculative execution, or service partitioning do not preserve behavior under real workloads, or if the smaller ecosystem and tooling maturity increase delivery risk.

Across five benchmarks and five baselines, Jac achieves a 1.8-8.7x reduction in AI-integration code relative to the OpenAI SDK, with competitive task quality and lower coding-agent development effort.
